the work (the gods' and then humans' forced labor); 'toil' where the line is about its weight. Note at Atrahasis 1:2
the work basket (the basket or frame for carrying earth, the badge of forced labor); gloss at first use in each part
the yoke (both words; abšānu the harness of a draft animal, note at Atrahasis 3:12)
a human being (the first, raw human; note at Atrahasis 3:9)
pâšu īpušamma izakkar ana (Akkadian speech formula)
X opened his mouth to speak, / and said to Y: (one line each, as the tablet has them)
throne-bearer / constable (titles of Ninurta and Ennugi)
We-ila (note at Atrahasis 2:11 and 3:48 on the readings We, Alla)
the holy woman (as Genesis 38:21 renders Hebrew qedeshah; note at Atrahasis 4:36)
Namtar (the plague god, a name meaning 'fate'); the common noun namtaru 'doom' (Atrahasis 6:7, with a note on the pun)
chills / sickness / head pain / the Asakku (a demon of disease; gloss at first use in each part)
kabātu D, 'be honored' / kabātu G, 'be heavy' (Atrahasis)
be honored / grow heavy (note at Atrahasis 4:8 on the Hebrew kaved/kavod root)
womb (note at Atrahasis 6:28: also 'compassion', like Hebrew rechem/rachamim)
roar (the land 'roared like a bull'; the heralds 'make the noise roar'), so the link shows
Dingirmah, kept as a name (Sumerian 'exalted deity', a title of Mami; note at Atrahasis 4:8)
the hairy ones (Enki's long-haired beings of the waters, his guards and messengers; note at Atrahasis 7:75)
shar (3,600, the big unit of counting by sixties; gloss at first use in each part)
a release / the yoke ('untied the yoke and set up a release', as Atrahasis 3:78 and 9:19)
oath ('the oath of the flood', Atrahasis 9:78)
the bolt and rope that lock in the sea (as Atrahasis 1:15)
minister (Nusku is Enlil's, Usmu is Enki's)
the flood (lower case, as in the Genesis Plain); 'the noise of the flood' (rigim abūbi), Atrahasis 11:18
the boat (never 'ark', which is the site's word for Noah's tevah); makūru, a god's processional barge, is also 'the boat' with a note (Atrahasis 12:30)
wall / reed wall ('Wall, listen to me closely! / Reed wall, guard every word I say!', Atrahasis 10:13-14; 'the reed wall' again at 12:40)
disaster (the flood's destruction of humankind: Atrahasis 11:12, 11:52, 12:16, 12:35, 12:94; one English word so the thread shows)
did not think it through (the charge against the gods and Enlil, Atrahasis 11:51; 12:15; 12:46 'without thinking')
